cases.observed_defect: `Yes, almost every day` gives `APPOSITION(Yes,day)`
cases.required_linguistic_correction: Affirmative minor speech act with temporal frequency, not noun apposition

cases.observed_defect: `Is my father in town?` has only POSSESSOR(father,my)
cases.required_linguistic_correction: Copular yes/no question with locative predicate

cases.observed_defect: They were hopeless of remedy lacks any semantic relation involving remedy
cases.required_linguistic_correction: Attach of remedy as argument/content of hopeless

cases.observed_defect: almost universal has no relation from almost to the universal attribute
cases.required_linguistic_correction: almost is a degree modifier of universal, not semantically omitted

cases.observed_defect: Mrs. Bennet's eyes sparkled has only AGENT(sparkled,eyes) and no Bennet possession
cases.required_linguistic_correction: Mrs Bennet is possessor of eyes, which are subject of sparkled

cases.observed_defect: `could not be long a secret`: `not` is unlinked
cases.required_linguistic_correction: Negative modal scope over `be ... a secret`

cases.observed_defect: to look at a picture is only MODIFIER(her,look) in called her to look
cases.required_linguistic_correction: her is object of called and controlled subject of look; picture object of look

cases.observed_defect: Darcy had walked away treats had as lexical V and ATTRIBUTE(had,walked)
cases.required_linguistic_correction: had is past perfect auxiliary of walked, with away/directional to-part PP

cases.observed_defect: POSSESSOR(praise,sister) misattaches of his sister's proficiency
cases.required_linguistic_correction: Sister is possessor of proficiency; proficiency is content of affectionate praise

cases.observed_defect: RECIPIENT(thanked,goodness) treats goodness as recipient of thanked
cases.required_linguistic_correction: him is recipient/addressee of thanked; for his goodness gives reason

cases.observed_defect: CONJUNCT(interest,nothing) conjoins an infinitival noun with negative proform, and nothing is not negated
cases.required_linguistic_correction: much to interest and nothing to justify inquiry are parallel objects and negative existential contrast

cases.observed_defect: `herself` is selected DEGREE, `at present` contains `present` V
cases.required_linguistic_correction: Reflexive object/complement and temporal `at present` PP

cases.observed_defect: or is selected N in or rather taller and APPOSITION(height,or)
cases.required_linguistic_correction: or rather taller is discourse correction of height comparison, not appositional noun

cases.observed_defect: RECIPIENT(thrown,open) treats open as noun object of was thrown open
cases.required_linguistic_correction: open is resultative predicate of door thrown, not recipient

cases.observed_defect: Quoted `“Oh! Mr. Collins!”` includes `Oh` PERSON; entire graph only has AGENT(began,Bennet), TOPIC(began,In)
cases.required_linguistic_correction: Source speech content tied to `began the projected conversation`, not discarded

cases.observed_defect: `had not mortified` has unlinked `not` and `had` V plus `mortified` ADJ
cases.required_linguistic_correction: Negative past-perfect predicate in the if-clause

cases.observed_defect: AGENT(called,by) makes the passive by-preposition the actor instead of the arrival
cases.required_linguistic_correction: the arrival of Saturday is causal agent of passive called, not lexical by

cases.observed_defect: CAUSE(mode,mode) is a self-loop on the same lexical semantic node
cases.required_linguistic_correction: as to the mode is a relational frame of curiosity, not mode causing itself

cases.observed_defect: `discourage his coming here so very often` treats `so` as N object; `should not remind` loses negation
cases.required_linguistic_correction: Possessive gerund subject, `so very often` degree adverb and negative modal scope

cases.observed_defect: had in Mr Bingley had been is selected V modifying Bingley rather than perfect auxiliary
cases.required_linguistic_correction: had auxiliary scopes over copula been and its predicative friend complement

cases.observed_defect: `offer to introduce` is selected with `offer` N, coordinated with `him`
cases.required_linguistic_correction: Verb `offer` coordinated with `entreat`, infinitive `to introduce` as its complement
